around.headline: Bengaluru techie arrested for allegedly filming landlady in bathroom
around.summary: A software professional was arrested after allegedly using a hidden camera to secretly film his landlady in her bathroom. Whenever you're in a new rented room or PG, do a quick visual sweep of the bathroom for odd fixtures, unusual holes, or small reflective lenses before settling in.

around.headline: HC calls Rs 5.3-crore job scam a 'classic potboiler', refuses to quash case
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court declined to quash a case tied to an alleged ₹5.3-crore job scam, calling the racket a "classic potboiler." Any job offer that demands upfront payment for a guaranteed placement is a red flag — verify directly with the company's official HR channel before paying anything.

around.headline: Trial traffic diversions begin around Madiwala to ease peak-hour rush
around.summary: Traffic police have started trial diversions around Madiwala from today to cut morning peak-hour congestion. If your commute passes through the area, check alternate routes before heading out.

around.headline: Karnataka resumes bike-taxi crackdown, seizes 263 vehicles, appeals to Supreme Court
around.summary: The state has resumed its crackdown on illegal bike taxis, seizing 263 two-wheelers and filing an appeal in the Supreme Court to keep the ban enforceable. If you rely on bike-taxi apps for your daily commute, expect disruptions and keep a backup transport option handy.

around.headline: Election Commission opens correction window for wrongly tagged voters in Karnataka
around.summary: The EC has opened a correction window for voters in Karnataka who were wrongly tagged during the ongoing electoral roll revision. Check your own and your family's voter status now and file a correction before the window closes.

around.headline: Centre revives push for delimitation, women's quota Bills; reaches out to Congress
around.summary: The central government has restarted efforts on delimitation and the women's reservation bill, engaging opposition parties including Congress. A delimitation exercise could eventually redraw parliamentary and assembly seat boundaries, including in Karnataka.

street_smart.title: You spot what looks like a tiny hidden camera in a rented bathroom — like today's case of a Bengaluru techie arrested for secretly filming his landlady.
street_smart.based_on: Today's news of a Bengaluru software professional arrested for allegedly using a hidden camera to film his landlady in her bathroom (The News Minute, The Hindu). Hidden-camera/voyeurism discovery hasn't been the street-smart topic in the last 3 weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: You've just moved into a new PG or rented flat. While settling in, you notice a small, oddly placed object near the bathroom mirror — a tiny reflective lens where there shouldn't be one, much like the hidden camera at the center of today's arrest case. What do you do?

choices.text: You're probably just imagining it — say nothing and carry on as usual.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Dismissing it means any recording keeps running unchecked, and you lose the narrow window where evidence and the device itself are still in place. Today's case only became an arrest because someone acted on the discovery.

choices.text: Rip the device out immediately and destroy it so it can't record anything more.
choices.feedback: Risky. Destroying the device also destroys the footage, storage card, and any fingerprints or metadata police need to identify who placed it and build a case — you could end up with no proof beyond your word.

choices.text: Confront the person you suspect directly, right now, before telling anyone else.
choices.feedback: Risky. A direct confrontation can tip off the person to wipe footage, remove other devices, or react unpredictably before you have any evidence or backup on record.

choices.text: Leave the device untouched, photograph it in place with your phone, and file a police complaint the same day (cyber-crime helpline 1930, or Karnataka's Women's helpline 1091).
choices.feedback: Correct. Photographing the device without moving it preserves it as evidence, and a same-day complaint gets police involved while the device and any footage are still traceable. Voyeurism is a criminal offence under IPC Section 354C and IT Act Section 66E.

takeaways: Never touch or remove a suspected hidden camera yourself — moving or destroying it can erase the evidence investigators need to trace the person responsible.
Photograph the device in place, then report it the same day via the national cyber-crime helpline (1930) or Karnataka's Women's helpline (1091).
In any new rented room, do a quick visual sweep of bathrooms and changing areas for unusual smoke detectors, clocks, or small reflective pinholes before you settle in.
